issues.display_title: Issue #453: API Detail Draft - Hotspot Mention Avatar
issues.main_description_html:
RESULT 07/07/26

✅ Implementation: API Detail Draft - Hotspot Mention Avatar

File Modified

  • src/Action/V1/Posts/DetailDraftPost.go

Technical Details

The API Detail Draft uses raw SQL mapped through GORM because draft posts bypass the standard views_timeline_post view.

To achieve the task requirements safely, we utilized split_part to extract the encrypt payload from the @[user](encrypt) string. This bypasses regex issues and ensures high reliability.

SQL Snippet Update

Inside the Go file, the hotspot SQL column subquery was updated to:

CASE 
  WHEN ph.type = 'mention' THEN 
    ph.data || jsonb_build_object(
      'avatar', (
        SELECT u.avatar 
        FROM users u 
        WHERE 
          (ph.data->>'username' LIKE '@[%](%)' AND u.encrypt = split_part(split_part(ph.data->>'username', '(', 2), ')', 1))
          OR 
          (ph.data->>'username' NOT LIKE '@[%](%)' AND u.username = ph.data->>'username')
        LIMIT 1
      )
    )
  ELSE ph.data 
END

This code snippet takes the JSONB data property and appends avatar: url to it whenever the hotspot type equals mention. The application automatically picks up the change upon next compile.

Objective

Support a new hotspot type mention inside panoramas/posts by dynamically attaching the mentioned user's avatar to the JSON response specifically for the Detail Draft Post endpoint.

Requirements

  1. Identify Mention Type: Look for type = 'mention' inside the post_hotspots JSON array.
  2. Handle Username Format: The username string is formatted like @[username](encrypt). We must extract the encrypt value securely using PostgreSQL string functions.
  3. Lookup Avatar: Query the users table where users.encrypt matches the extracted encrypt string. Fallback to matching users.username directly if the @[username](encrypt) format is missing.
  4. Append Avatar to Hotspot: Concatenate the resulting avatar URL into the existing data JSON object of the hotspot before returning it to the client.

Target Area

  • src/Action/V1/Posts/DetailDraftPost.go

issues.display_title: Issue #456: Timeline View - Hotspot Mention Avatar
issues.main_description_html:
RESULT 07/07/26

✅ Implementation: Timeline View - Hotspot Mention Avatar

Technical Details

This change introduces data manipulation at the Database View Level so that the API application has no additional processing overhead.

By utilizing PostgreSQL's split_part string function, we reliably extract the unique encrypt hash and map it against the panorra_dev.public.users table.

DDL Update Snippet

The following logic was injected into the hotspot JSONB aggregation sub-select inside views_timeline_post:

CASE 
  WHEN ph.type = 'mention' THEN 
    ph.data || jsonb_build_object(
      'avatar', (
        SELECT u.avatar 
        FROM panorra_dev.public.users u 
        WHERE 
          (ph.data->>'username' LIKE '@[%](%)' AND u.encrypt = split_part(split_part(ph.data->>'username', '(', 2), ')', 1))
          OR 
          (ph.data->>'username' NOT LIKE '@[%](%)' AND u.username = ph.data->>'username')
        LIMIT 1
      )
    )
  ELSE ph.data 
END

Deployment Note

Unlike Go application code which runs on execution, this SQL file must be applied directly to the PostgreSQL database to recreate public.views_timeline_post. You must copy the contents of DDL_views_timeline_post.sql and run it against the target database (panorra_dev).

Objective

Support a new hotspot type mention inside panoramas/posts by dynamically attaching the mentioned user's avatar to the JSON response at the database view level.

Background

The views_timeline_post view powers multiple core GET endpoints, including Timeline, Detail Post, and Most Popular Posts. Updating this view is critical for displaying the user's avatar when they are mentioned in a panorama hotspot on any public-facing API request.

Requirements

  1. Identify Mention Type: Detect type = 'mention' inside the post_hotspots data structure during the SELECT view compilation.
  2. Extract Encrypt String: ph.data->>'username' holds a formatted tag string like @[royalecheese](vc473434aaf). Extract the vc473434aaf portion dynamically.
  3. Lookup Avatar: Join or query the panorra_dev.public.users table matching the extracted encrypt hash. Keep a fallback for plaintext usernames.
  4. Append Avatar: Append the retrieved avatar field to the JSON structure aggregated into the hotspot column.

Target Area

  • docs/migrations/views/DDL_views_timeline_post.sql

RESULT 07/07/26

✅ Implementation: API Search Folder Bookmark Published

Example Search Published Folder Bookmark API

Endpoint: GET /search/published-folder-bookmark
Description: Retrieves a list of publicly published folder bookmarks from all creators. This endpoint powers the Bookmark tab in the Search Discover page, providing infinite scroll capabilities, full-text search, and category filtering.

Example cURL Request

curl -G "http://localhost:3000/search/published-folder-bookmark" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <your_token>" \
  --data-urlencode "page=1" \
  --data-urlencode "limit=10" \
  --data-urlencode "q=holiday" \
  --data-urlencode "category=0" \
  --data-urlencode "include=slug,name,thumbnail,user,total_bookmark"

Request Parameters

  • page (int, optional): Page number for pagination. Defaults to 1.
  • limit (int, optional): Number of items per page. Defaults to 8.
  • q (string, optional): Keyword to search published folders by name. (Also supports name as an alias for backward compatibility).
  • category (int, optional): Filter by category_id. Passing 0 or omitting it skips the category filter.
  • include (string, optional): Comma-separated list of fields to include in the response (e.g., slug,name,user). Using this limits the output only to the specified fields.
  • include (allowed): ("slug", "name", "description", "location", "location_name", "category_name", "published_at", "total_bookmark", "thumbnail", "user", "potd")

Success Response

The response includes the folder details along with nested user, geo location, and a strictly formatted total_bookmark object.

{
  "statusCode": 200,
  "data": {
    "valid": true,
    "version": 0,
    "messages": "Search Published Folder Bookmarks",
    "bookmarks": [
      {
        "slug": "holiday-places-2024",
        "name": "Holiday Places",
        "description": "Places to visit",
        "location": {
            "lat": -8.409518, 
            "lng": 115.188919
        },
        "location_name": "Bali",
        "category_name": "Leisure",
        "published_at": "2024-01-01T00:00:00Z",
        "potd": false,
        "total_bookmark": {
            "counter_bookmak": 5
        },
        "thumbnail": "sample.jpg",
        "user": {
            "username": "tester",
            "avatar": "avatar.jpg",
            "encrypt": "abcd123"
        }
      }
    ]
  }
}

Error Responses

Unauthorized (User context invalid or missing):

{
  "statusCode": 401,
  "data": {
    "error": "Unauthorized"
  }
}

Internal Server Error (Database connection failure):

{
  "statusCode": 500,
  "data": {
    "error": "Internal Server Error"
  }
}

Overview

This implementation addresses Github Task #450 ("Update API Search Bookmark") by creating a dedicated endpoint rather than modifying the existing SearchFolderBookmark logic. This ensures that the current user's bookmark searching logic remains intact while providing the Frontend with a specialized endpoint for the "Search Discover" page to query publicly published bookmarks globally.

Files Created/Modified

  1. src/Action/V1/Search/SearchPublishedFolderBookmark.go (New File)
  2. src/Controllers/V1/SearchControllers.go (Modified)
  3. src/Routes/V1/SearchRoutes.go (Modified)
  4. src/Models/SearchModel.go (Modified - Added SearchFolderBookmark struct)

Technical Details

1. New Endpoint Route

  • Path: GET /search/published-folder-bookmark
  • Controller: SearchPublishedFolderBookmark

2. Querying Strategy

Instead of querying the base folder_bookmark table filtered by the current user (user_id = ?), the new logic queries the views_published_folders PostgreSQL view. This satisfies the requirement to "Discover publicly published bookmarks from all creators".

3. Filters and Parameters Supported

  • q (and name as fallback): Used to perform an ILIKE search against the folder name.
  • category: When provided (and not 0), filters the folders strictly to the requested category_id.
  • page & limit: Used to paginate results for infinite scrolling on the frontend.
  • Implicitly orders by published_at DESC for a "recent list" output when query params are empty.

4. Struct and Response Formatting

A new struct SearchFolderBookmark was added to Models/SearchModel.go. It facilitates mapping the flat structure of the views_published_folders view into the nested JSON objects required by the frontend:

  • Owner Mapping: owner_username, owner_avatar, and owner_encrypt are grouped into a user JSON payload.
  • Geo-Location: The location JSONB field is passed directly to the response to support map markers.
  • Bookmark Count: The total_bookmark integer from the view is re-formatted in code to a JSON object ({"counter_bookmak": <value>}) to strictly match legacy formatting without needing to trigger extra ElasticSearch queries during the loop.

Security Considerations

Blocked users, deactivated users, and the requester's own privacy settings (e.g. blockUser, deactiveUser) are still respected by actively filtering out folders where owner_encrypt IN (?).

Description

  • New flow: bookmark publish from search pages.

file brainstorming

search-bookmark-integration-brainstorming.md

Frontend Integration Notes (from brainstorming)

Source: docs/brainstorming/search-bookmark-integration-brainstorming.md (panorra-pwa) · UI design: panorra-pwa#3107 (Create Search Discover Layout)

What this powers (FE): the Bookmark tab of the new Search Discover page (#3107) — a Feed-First Search Sidebar with Post · Bookmark · User · Hashtag tabs, category filters (All / Leisure / Real Estate / Business), a scrollable results sidebar over the map. It must be useful before typing (show recent bookmarks on open) and re-query on debounced search + category change.

⚠️ Please confirm (BE) — meaning of "bookmark publish"

The one-line description is ambiguous; the FE integration branches on which of these it is:

  • (a) Search the current user's own bookmark folders from the search page, where "publish" = a broadcast action per folder.
  • (b) Discover publicly published bookmarks from all creators (the FE's working assumption).
  • (c) Search results just gain a publish/bookmark-state flag to render.

Expected endpoint contract (FE will consume)

  • Search Bookmark endpoint returning list items for the tab, supporting: q (query), category, page / limit (pagination for infinite scroll), and empty query = recent list.
  • Response should include, per bookmark item: id/slug, title/name, thumbnail, owner/creator, counts, and (if geo) latitude/longitude for map markers — plus any publish state field the tab needs.
  • Please document the exact path, params, and response shape so the FE mapper can be finalized (envelope keys verified against a live response).

FE plan (summary)

  • New pages-new/search/ feature: search.facade.searchBookmarks(query, category, page) → this endpoint → runDecryption → search-bookmark.mapper → signal → cards + map markers. Signals, OnPush, no any.
  • States: recent (no query) · debounced search · category filter · loading · empty · error · infinite scroll. "Publish" affordance implemented only if scoped per the clarification above (reusing the existing broadcast / sharedPostData mechanism).

Full context, approaches, risks, and success criteria are in the linked brainstorming doc.

RESULT 07/07/26

✅ Implementation: Search Post Updates (Description & Include)

Overview

This document outlines the implementation details for enhancing the SearchPost API with structured description formatting and a dynamic include filtering parameter.

Files Modified

  1. src/Models/PostsModel.go
  2. src/Action/V1/Search/SearchPost.go

Technical Details

1. Struct Updates (Models/PostsModel.go)

  • Appended Description, ShortDescription, and LongDescription to the SearchPost struct.
  • ShortDescription and LongDescription were given the gorm:"-" tag to prevent GORM from attempting to query them directly from the database schema since they are dynamically computed.

2. Description Formatting (SearchPost.go)

  • Imported html and panorra-api-go/src/Utils/Functions/PostFunctions.
  • After successfully querying the database via .Scan(), a loop iterates through the results.
  • For each post with a non-empty description, html.UnescapeString() is called to decode HTML entities, followed by PostFunctions.WrapText() which generates the structured short and long representations natively.

3. Dynamic Field Filtering (include)

  • Strict Boundaries: Defined an allowedFields array consisting exclusively of the 18 fields that the API historically returned (e.g., slug, location_name, animation, etc.). This satisfies the requirement of strictly not leaking new fields.
  • Query Extraction: c.Query("include") extracts the raw parameter.
  • include allowed: ("slug", "thumbnail", "panorama_preview", "panorama_quality", "post_type", "animation", "animation_filter", "little_planet", "little_planet_filter", "pending", "potd", "fullname", "username", "avatar", "broadcast_data", "location_name", "location_post", "description")
  • Validation: Filtered the raw parameter against the whitelist using Functions.GetValidIncludes(include, allowedFields).
  • SQL Optimization:
    • Instead of a hardcoded .Select("..."), the query.Select() is dynamically joined based on the validFields array.
    • An underlying rule injects the slug identifier if it was missing to guarantee core operations and struct bindings don't break.
  • Payload Optimization:
    • The final struct array is no longer dumped straight to the JSON response when include is present.
    • A nested loop maps the struct properties to a map[string]interface{} dictionary.
    • This ensures that fields absent from the include param are entirely stripped out from the HTTP payload, drastically reducing data transfer footprint.

Objective

Enhance the /search/post endpoint (src/Action/V1/Search/SearchPost.go) to support dynamic payload filtering via the include query parameter and standardized description formatting, matching the behavior of existing Post APIs (e.g., TimelinePostRecent).

Requirements

1. Description Formatting

  • The current implementation directly returns description without parsing.
  • We need to parse and generate short_description and long_description from the description string using PostFunctions.WrapText().
  • The SearchPost struct in Models/PostsModel.go must be updated to accommodate these new fields.

2. Dynamic Field Filtering (include)

  • Support the include query parameter to allow frontend clients to selectively fetch necessary fields.
  • Strict Constraint: Do not expose or allow querying of any new fields that weren't already present in the original SELECT query. The inclusion logic must be bounded by the original 18 fields (slug, thumbnail, description, username, location_name, etc).
  • Use Functions.GetValidIncludes(include, allowedFields) to sanitize the request.
  • Optimize the SQL Select query to only fetch valid fields from the database, minimizing DB load.
  • Filter the final JSON response to strictly contain only the requested keys.
